title: Runtime: fetch + cache quantization profiles, run compat checks, and safely fall back to baseline
creator: Noah Patel
description:
Goal
Implement the serving-runtime codepath to resolve the correct quantization profile per request, fetch profile artifacts from the model registry, cache them safely (multi-tenant, multi-GPU), validate compatibility (GPU arch + kernel/runtime constraints), and ensure we always fall back to baseline (fp16/bf16) execution when anything is incompatible/unavailable.

Why
Quantization profiles will be opt-in and route-scoped. Runtime must be able to:
- Resolve profile deterministically (model_id + profile_id/version + hardware scope)
- Avoid introducing tail latency regressions due to registry fetches
- Prevent outages when profiles are mis-scoped or kernels aren’t available on a worker
- Provide observability breadcrumbs for routing/SRE to quickly disable profiles by route/customer

Scope
1) Profile resolution + fetch
- Input signals (runtime-side): model identifier (resolved model version), requested quantization policy outcome from route config (e.g., disabled / enabled / canary), and worker hardware fingerprint.
- Fetch the profile manifest + artifacts from model registry (internal endpoint; see registry PRs).
- Support both "latest compatible" and "pinned version" semantics (pinned preferred for early beta). If "latest compatible" is requested, runtime must still select a concrete version and include it in per-request tags.

2) Caching
- Maintain an in-process cache keyed by: (profile_id, profile_version, runtime_build, gpu_arch, kernel_backend).
- Cache entries include:
  - profile manifest (validated)
  - resolved artifact URIs and digests
  - compiled/loaded kernel handles or quantization engine handles (where applicable)
  - an expiration / refresh policy
- Must prevent cache stampede when many workers refresh simultaneously (singleflight / request coalescing + backoff).
- Cache invalidation triggers:
  - explicit version change from control plane (preferred)
  - TTL expiry (safety net)
  - registry "profile revoked" signal (future; stub now)

3) Compatibility checks (hard fail -> fallback)
Checks must be deterministic and conservative; do not attempt partial quantization.
- GPU architecture: e.g., sm80/sm90 scoping.
- Kernel backend compatibility: e.g., "triton", "cutlass", "vendor_int8".
- Runtime build constraints: minimum runtime version / feature flags.
- Model family constraints: only apply if model architecture matches profile metadata (avoid accidentally applying a llama profile to mistral-like variants).
- Sequence length regime constraints: if profile only validated for <= N context, runtime can decline when request exceeds N (or treat as "unknown" and fallback). For v1 we should fallback to baseline to avoid quality/perf surprises.

4) Safe fallback behavior
Fallback must be silent to the customer (no 4xx) unless they explicitly request a profile via a strict header (not planned for v1).
- If fetch fails (timeout, 5xx, missing artifact): run baseline.
- If manifest validation fails: run baseline + emit error log + counter.
- If incompatibility is detected: run baseline + emit incompatibility reason tag.
- If load/initialization fails: run baseline and mark cache entry as "bad" with a cooldown (don’t retry every request).

5) Observability hooks (runtime-side; not full dashboards)
- Emit counters/histograms tagged with: model_id, profile_id, profile_version, execution_mode (quantized|baseline), fallback_reason.
- Add structured logs at WARN (incompatibility) / ERROR (fetch/validation/load failure) with request_id + route_id when available.
- Ensure tags are low-cardinality where possible; profile_version is allowed, but avoid raw artifact URIs.

Implementation notes / current approach
- Add ProfileResolver interface in runtime serving path after model selection and before kernel selection.
- Resolver returns either QuantizedExecutionPlan or BaselineExecutionPlan.
- Implement RegistryClient with:
  - request timeout <= 150ms (configurable)
  - retries: 1 retry max with jitter; do not exceed budget
  - circuit breaker: open on sustained 5xx to avoid self-DDoS
- Cache layer uses singleflight per cache key, with negative caching for known-bad profiles (cooldown 5m).

Acceptance criteria
- No functional regression when quantization is disabled (baseline path unchanged).
- When quantization is enabled but profile is missing/incompatible, requests succeed and run baseline.
- Under load test with 1k workers starting simultaneously, registry QPS remains bounded (demonstrate stampede prevention).
- Worker supports mixed traffic across multiple routes/models without cross-tenant leakage in cache keys.
- Clear metrics for: profile_fetch_success, profile_fetch_failure, profile_incompatible, profile_load_failure, quantized_requests, baseline_fallback_requests.

Out of scope
- Automatic always-on quantization decisions (policy engine owns).
- User-supplied profiles.
- Cross-worker shared cache (e.g., Redis); in-process only for MVP.

Security considerations
- Runtime must verify registry-provided artifact digests/signatures before loading.
- Do not log raw signed URLs or credentials.
- Ensure permissions: runtime identity can read profiles but cannot publish.

Links
- Runtime PR (WIP): sources/github/redwood/pr_28766_runtime_fetch_and_cache_profiles.json
- Fallback hardening PR (related): sources/github/redwood/pr_28805_fallback_to_baseline_on_incompatibility.json
- Cache stampede hotfix (follow-up): sources/github/redwood/pr_28925_hotfix_guard_against_profile_cache_stampede.json
- Registry layout: sources/github/redwood-model-registry/pr_912_add_profile_artifact_layout_and_manifest.json

Test plan
- Unit tests:
  - cache keying + singleflight
  - manifest validation failures -> fallback
  - incompat checks by gpu_arch/model_family/runtime_version
  - negative cache cooldown behavior
- Integration tests:
  - fake registry returning profile variants across sm80/sm90
  - simulate registry timeout -> baseline
  - simulate incompatible kernel backend -> baseline
- Load test:
  - cold start with N workers; assert registry QPS bound + p95 latency impact within budget

Rollout
- Behind feature flag: runtime.quant_profiles.enabled (default off)
- Shadow mode option: resolve + fetch + metrics, but execute baseline (helps validate compatibility matrix without quality risk)

Open questions
- Do we want to allow "best-effort" quantization for long-context requests (e.g., int8 only) or always fallback? Proposed: always fallback in v1.
- For "latest compatible" selection, should selection be done by registry (server-side) or runtime (client-side)? Proposed: registry server-side for consistency; runtime only verifies.

comments: 2025-01-16 (Hiro Tanaka): Please ensure compat checks include kernel backend + minimum driver/runtime. We’ve seen sm80 machines with older driver stacks fail certain int8 paths; better to gate and fallback than crash. I’ll send the backend identifier list we want to standardize on.

2025-01-22 (Quentin Harris): Registry manifest will include: model_family, allowed_gpu_arches, required_runtime_semver, kernel_backend, artifact_digests. Signature verification API is ready on the client; docs incoming. Please don’t rely on artifact filename conventions beyond what’s in the manifest.

2025-01-29 (Mateo Alvarez): Implemented singleflight + negative caching (5m cooldown) and added a 150ms fetch budget. Added WARN logs for incompatibility and ERROR for validation/load failures. Next: tighten cache keying to include kernel backend + runtime build hash to avoid cross-release reuse.

2025-02-03 (Sean Gallagher): From SRE side, please make sure fallback reasons are machine-parsable (enum) so we can alert on spikes (e.g., incompatible_sm_arch vs fetch_timeout). Also confirm we can flush caches during rollback (even if it’s just a SIGHUP endpoint).

2025-02-06 (Noah Patel): Reviewed PR 28766. Main ask: (1) ensure we never block request path waiting on a slow fetch if baseline is available; (2) add circuit breaker to avoid thundering herd when registry has partial outage; (3) add a lightweight admin endpoint to invalidate a specific (profile_id, version) cache entry for incident response.
